text: CITY ATTORNEY'S IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE O
Measure O would authorize the City to issue up to $ in general obligation bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, and improvement of the following:

Acquisition of land for a civic center that would consist of (l) an approximately 20,000 square foot police department, including an emergency operations center, and (2) an approximately 100,000 square foot building to house a public library, City Hall, and related civic and community facilities;

Water system infrastructure projects, including water storage facilities, water mains, distribution pipelines, and related facilities and improvements necessary to improve system reliability, capacity, resiliency, and long-term service delivery;

Stormwater system infrastructure projects, including storm drains and related facilities and improvements necessary to improve drainage capacity, flood protection, water quality, and system reliability; and
Acquisition of land for recreational facilities and park improvements, including a track and field facility and related park amenities.

The bonds would be payable from ad valorem taxes levied on taxable property in the City. The maximum interest rate to be paid on the bonds shall not exceed 12%, though the prevailing interest rates could be less. The City estimates that the highest tax rate that would be required to be levied is approximately $114.41 per $100,000 of assessed value, which the City projects would begin to apply in fiscal year 2028-2029. The City also estimates that the average annual tax rate that would be required to be levied is $105.26 per $100,000 of assessed value, with the final fiscal year in which the tax would be collected being 2057-2058. The City also estimates that the total debt service, including the principal and interest, that would be required to be repaid if all the bonds are issued and sold is $268,205,658.

Bond proceeds would be deposited into a separate fund and may be used only for the public improvements described in the measure. All expenditures would be subject to an annual independent financial audit and the City's Director of Finance would be required to file a report with the City Council at least annually showing the amount of bond proceeds collected and expended and the status of the improvements.
It may be possible for the City to leverage private donations and state and federal grants to help finance these improvements if the bonds are issued.
This measure was placed on the ballot by the City Council of the City of East Palo Alto. It requires a two-thirds vote to pass.
Voting "Yes" would mean authorizing the City to issue up to $125,000,000 in general obligation bonds for use on the public improvements stated in the measure and briefly summarized above.
Voting "No" would mean the City would not be authorized to issue the bonds.
John D. Lé City Attorney

text: Argument Against East Palo Alto $125,000,000 Bond Issue, Measure When voters are asked to go into debt with bond measures like Measure what are they saying? They are admitting that everything in the current budget is more ilnportant than the projects listed in this ballot measure. Budgets reflect priorities. Actions speak louder than words: every tax dollar spent today is going to something they consider a higher priority than "replacing deteriorating water pipes to provide safe/ clean drinking water" and "constructing a Library." Do you agree? A bond is much like a mortgage. When you buy a home, truth in lending laws mandate that banks must tell the real cost (the loan amount AND 30 years of interest payments). $ 125,000,000 could cost us $250,000,000 or more (depending on the interests' rates). Shouldn't consumer protection laws apply to bond debt too? We deserve to know the full truth about Measure . We don't even know when this debt will begin, nor what market interest rate will be, when it does. Shouldn't consumer protection laws apply to bond measures? Taxpayers deserve all the full facts. We do not know when this debt will begin, or what the market interest rate will be at that time. Which is more important to you? 1. Paying for essential safety repairs u,g_!!, by using dollars already in the budgetl. 2. Sending new tax dollars in the form of principal and interest paynwnts -- to big banks, investment brokers, and other wealthy people, for use in tax shelters. Is #2 really the best use of our taxes? If you value clean drinking water more than funding tax shelters with tax free bonds, vote NO on Measure If you value clean water more than making interest payments for 25 years, vote NO on Measure More information, www.SVTaxpayers.org

text: East Palo Alto's future should be decided by the people who live here — not out-of-town special interest opponents who don't represent us. WE CAN'T AFFORD TO WAIT. East Palo Alto residents know what our community needs: safe drinking water, reliable infrastructure, safe places for our children and teens, and facilities that are ready when emergencies strike. YES on "O": • Replaces deteriorating drinking water pipes. • Repairs aging storm drains to prevent neighborhood flooding/pollution. • Upgrades community facilities for earthquake safety. • Ensures adequate water storage and a modern Emergency Command Center. Delaying these needs and repairs will only be more expensive in the future. OUR KIDS AND TEENS DESERVE BETTER. East Palo Alto's library is undersized and overcrowded, without adequate space for literacy and children's programs. YES on "O" creates a modern library, including spaces where children/teens can safely gather and learn. These major projects can't be funded by the City's budget without taking millions from other essential services on which local families rely. YES on "0" IS TRANSPARENT/ACCOUNTABLE By law, Measure O ALL funds can ONLY be spent on the services specified. Read the official Measure O language at https://www.cityofepa.org/clerk/page/city-elections-0. All spending must be transparently disclosed and publicly posted. These Transparency/Accountability provisions ensure funds are spent efficiently, effectively and as promised. Independent oversight and annual audits are an additional layer of checks and balances. Vote YES on "O" for our kids and teens, our water, our safety, and the entire East Palo Alto Community.
SAN MATEO COUNTY
LECTIONS OFFICER BY: LERK
